clue.text: Flash clues regularly amuse

parts.note: a flash, as in 'back in a flash', is an instant, also called a tick

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter of the word clues, here the second and fourth

explanation.surface: Someone finds that brief, flashing clues are a source of amusement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flash' looks like a burst of light, but here it means a moment, as in 'back in a tick', the British phrase for a very short time.
explanation.definitionFit: To tickle someone is to entertain or delight them, as in 'tickled pink'.

clue.text: In Calabria, perhaps riot's dispersed (one loitering covered in shell)

indicators.note: In at the start says the dispersed letters go into the region word

parts.note: Calabria is the toe of the boot-shaped Italian peninsula, so it is an example of a toe

indicators.note: dispersed says the letters of riots are scattered and reordered

parts.note: the s counts as a letter here

explanation.surface: Riots break up in southern Italy, a sentence wrapped round an aside about a slow traveller.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' looks like a link to Calabria but is the container signal. Calabria is the region forming the toe of Italy's boot.
explanation.definitionFit: A tortoise is a slow-moving reptile carrying a hard protective carapace on its back.

clue.text: Check soup, cooking up the traditional eastern dish

parts.note: CH is an abbreviation for check, as in chess

indicators.note: cooking means the letters of soup are mixed into a new order
in a down clue, up means the next piece reads bottom to top

parts.note: ye is the old way of writing the, as in 'ye olde'

explanation.surface: A cook checks the soup while preparing a classic Oriental dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooking' turns SOUP into OPSU, and 'up' turns YE (old 'the') into EY.
explanation.definitionFit: Chop suey is a Chinese-American stir-fry of meat and vegetables served in restaurants.

clue.text: Part of leaf left on decoration

parts.note: the OBE, Order of the British Empire, is an honour or decoration

explanation.surface: A medal left lying on a leaf.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' in a down clue puts L above OBE.
explanation.definitionFit: A lobe is a rounded projection or division of a leaf's blade, as in an oak.

clue.text: One opening pizzeria strangely can't eat food there?

indicators.note: the one letter that opens the word pizzeria is its first
strangely says the letters of can't eat are rearranged

parts.note: the apostrophe is ignored, leaving seven letters

explanation.surface: A diner at a pizzeria finds, oddly, they cannot eat anything.
explanation.walkthrough: 'there' points back to the pizzeria, so the definition depends on the surface's own setting.
explanation.definitionFit: Pancetta, Italian cured belly pork, is a common pizza topping, so it is food found at a pizzeria.

clue.text: Cinephile's cryptic clues could characterise this

definitions.text: Cinephile's cryptic clues could characterise this

parts.words: Cinephile's cryptic clues could characterise this
parts.note: the words cinephile's, cryptic, clues, could and characterise all begin with the same hard c sound, a repetition the clue both names and shows

explanation.surface: A film buff's crossword clues might be described in a certain way.
explanation.walkthrough: Cinephile was a pseudonym used in the FT by the setter Araucaria, so it looks like a reference to his style, but the clue simply shows its own repeated opening sounds.
explanation.definitionFit: Repetition of the same initial consonant across neighbouring words is the literary device in question.

clue.text: Prawn, perhaps reddish-brown, one keeps in container

indicators.note: one keeps in container means the colour and one words are held inside the container word

parts.note: a can is a container
rust is a reddish-brown colour
an ace is a one in cards

explanation.surface: A reddish-brown prawn is kept in a tin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' says a prawn is one example.
explanation.definitionFit: Prawns belong to the class of hard-shelled aquatic arthropods along with crabs and lobsters.

clue.text: Oriental place starts to test an Indian pasty

indicators.note: starts to takes the opening letter of each of the next three words

parts.note: pasty means pale-faced, which is wan

explanation.surface: Someone sets out to sample an Indian pasty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pasty' looks like the pastry snack, but it is the adjective meaning pale.
explanation.definitionFit: Taiwan is an island country off the east coast of China, so a place in the Far East.

clue.text: Sat with Tom, spinning tops

indicators.note: spinning says the letters of Sat and Tom are whirled into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone sat with Tom watching spinning tops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tops' looks like the toy, but it means a maximum.
explanation.definitionFit: At most means no more than, the upper limit, as in 'it costs ten pounds at most'.

clue.text: House doctor in US state giving lozenges perhaps

indicators.note: in places the house and doctor letters inside the state abbreviation

parts.note: RI is the postal abbreviation for Rhode Island
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's qualification

explanation.surface: A house doctor practising in an American state prescribes lozenges.
explanation.walkthrough: 'House' is not the TV doctor House; it gives HO, and MB is the doctor. 'perhaps' marks lozenges as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: A rhombus is the diamond shape, also called a lozenge, so lozenges are examples of the plural shape.

clue.text: Stuff washing up! Uniform, at front, visibly covered in onion, garlic, etc

indicators.note: covered in says the uniform letter and the front of visibly sit inside the plant genus

parts.note: Allium is the plant genus of onions, garlic, leeks and chives
U is Uniform in the NATO phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: at front takes the opening letter of the word visibly

explanation.surface: Kitchen chaos: a uniform visibly smeared with onion and garlic needs a wash-up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'covered in' puts UV (U for Uniform, V opening 'visibly') inside ALLIUM. 'washing up' sounds like kitchen work, but it means carried in and dropped by water.
explanation.definitionFit: Alluvium is silt and sediment that rivers carry and leave on the land, material brought by water.

clue.text: Sporting event making revolutionary progress

parts.note: a cycle race whose wheels revolve as it makes a progress, a journey round the country of the 1789 Revolution

explanation.surface: A sporting contest moves forward in a radical way.
explanation.walkthrough: A progress is an old word for a ceremonial journey; 'revolutionary' points both at turning wheels and at France's revolution.
explanation.definitionFit: The famous multi-stage bicycle race lapping round France each July, with constantly turning wheels.

clue.text: Seashore less cold, drier in Kent?

indicators.note: less means the cold letter is taken away from the shore word

parts.note: the seashore is the coast
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: A beach without the chill is a drier place in Kent.
explanation.walkthrough: Kent, a county in south-east England, is famous for oast houses, kilns for drying hops; the question mark says it is one example.
explanation.definitionFit: An oast is a kiln for drying hops, a familiar sight across the Kent countryside.

clue.text: Items of footwear distributed to top brass

indicators.note: distributed says the letters of to top brass are spread around and reordered

explanation.surface: Boots are handed out to the senior officers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'distributed' rearranges TOTOPBRASS. 'top brass' reads as the senior officers, but it is only letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Bootstraps are the loops sewn on boots for pulling them on, parts belonging to footwear.

clue.text: One caught by PC, splitting half with low life?

definitions.text: One caught by PC, splitting half with low life?

parts.note: A is the indefinite article, meaning one
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

indicators.note: half takes the front half of the word the abbreviation PC stands for

parts.note: PC stands for personal computer
lice are parasites, about the lowest of life forms

explanation.surface: A partner in crime is nabbed by a police constable after sharing the takings with a criminal.
explanation.walkthrough: PC looks like a police constable but gives COMPUTER, of which 'half' keeps COMP; 'splitting' is a link. Read whole, the clue describes the answer: a crook's partner, sharing the loot, who gets arrested.
explanation.definitionFit: An accomplice is a partner in crime who helps a wrongdoer and expects a share of the takings.

clue.text: Observe, around racing car centre, old US actor

indicators.note: around says the spy word wraps round the rearranged letters

parts.note: to observe is to spy

indicators.note: racing says the letters of car centre are rearranged

explanation.surface: A spectator watches a racing car at the centre of the track, alongside a veteran American film star.
explanation.walkthrough: 'racing car' looks like one thing, but 'racing' is the anagram signal and 'around' wraps the result.
explanation.definitionFit: Spencer Tracy was a Hollywood star of the 1930s to 1960s, twice an Oscar winner.

clue.text: Geed wild horse on to hostile battleground

indicators.note: wild says the letters of Geed are jumbled

parts.note: horse is slang for heroin, abbreviated H
ill can mean unfriendly or hostile, as in ill will

explanation.surface: A rider urges a wild horse on towards hostile ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on to' sets the horse and hostile pieces after the jumbled letters. Edgehill in Warwickshire was the first major battle of the English Civil War, in 1642.
explanation.definitionFit: Edgehill was the site of the opening pitched fight of the English Civil War.

clue.text: Tall one (French) on Ilkley, ram bling

parts.note: un is French for one

indicators.note: split differently these words read rambling, suggesting the letters of Ilkley wander into a new order

explanation.surface: A tall French visitor on Ilkley Moor, with a ram wearing jewellery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ram bling' is 'rambling' split in two, the anagram signal for ILKLEY. Ilkley is a Yorkshire town famous for its moor. 'Tall' means far-fetched, as in a tall story.
explanation.definitionFit: A tall story is an improbable one, hard to believe.

clue.text: Railway out of Midlands city created danger somewhere in London

indicators.note: out of means the railway letters are removed from the city name

parts.note: Coventry is a city in the English Midlands

indicators.note: created suggests making something new from the letters of danger

explanation.surface: A railway line leading out of a Midlands city is said to have caused danger in London.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of' takes RY from COVENTRY, and 'created' rearranges DANGER as GARDEN. Covent Garden is a market and theatre district in central London.
explanation.definitionFit: Covent Garden is a district in the West End, known for its piazza and opera house.

clue.text: Sci-fi writer lifted award during endorsement

indicators.note: in a down clue, lifted means everything is read from bottom to top
during says the award letters come within the endorsement word

parts.note: a visa is an endorsement stamped in a passport
the OM, Order of Merit, is a British award

explanation.surface: A science-fiction author picks up an award in the middle of an endorsement deal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lifted' turns the whole assembly upwards, so the full word reads bottom to top in the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: Isaac Asimov wrote the Foundation and robot stories, a giant of science fiction.

clue.text: One behaves nervously giving currency in notes

indicators.note: in means the currency word sits inside the two notes letters

parts.note: n is a standard abbreviation for note, so notes gives two of them
the euro is a currency

explanation.surface: Someone acts jumpy while handing over money in banknotes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'behaves nervously' looks like jittery behaviour, but it means works as part of the nervous system. 'notes' gives N and N, n being short for note.
explanation.definitionFit: A nerve cell transmits signals through the body, literally doing the work of the nervous system.

clue.text: Head of production involved in casting the person here?

indicators.note: involved in says the letter from production sits inside the rearranged letters
casting suggests throwing the letters of the person into a new order
the head of the word production is its first letter

explanation.surface: A head of production is busy casting for a role on set.
explanation.walkthrough: 'casting' rearranges THEPERSON, and 'involved in' adds P (the head of 'production'). 'casting' doubles as the film sense; Shepperton Studios are near London, where films are cast and shot.
explanation.definitionFit: Shepperton is home to major film studios, the very place where a production does its casting.

clue.text: Mike's spent a grand refurbishing house

indicators.note: refurbishing suggests rearranging the letters once the grand has been spent

parts.note: the possessive s counts as a letter here
K is a thousand, as in a grand

explanation.surface: Mike has spent a thousand pounds doing up his house.
explanation.walkthrough: MIKES less K ('spent a grand') leaves MIES, which 'refurbishing' rearranges. A semi is a semi-detached house, very common in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: A semi is short for a semi-detached dwelling, one sharing a wall with its neighbour.

clue.text: Fruit, two picked up

indicators.note: picked up means heard, so the word for two is taken by its sound

parts.note: a pair is two

explanation.surface: Two pieces of fruit are gathered.
explanation.definitionFit: A pear is a sweet orchard fruit, the sort grown on trees alongside apples.

clue.text: Rocky going west on major road, with constant sheep

indicators.note: in an across clue, going west means the whole string of pieces is read from right to left

parts.note: taken as written
the A1 is Britain's longest numbered road, written AI
C is the usual symbol for a constant, such as the speed of light
a ram is a male sheep

explanation.surface: A boxer heads west along a main road with a flock of sheep.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going west' reverses ON + AI + C + RAM, giving the answer. The A1 is Britain's main north-south road. Rocky looks like rough terrain, but it is the boxer's first name.
explanation.definitionFit: Rocky Marciano was the undefeated American heavyweight boxing champion of the 1950s.

clue.text: City flooded, failing to barricade quarters

indicators.note: to barricade means to shut in, so the vice word encloses the quarters letters

parts.note: a failing is a vice, a moral weakness
E and N are compass points, two of the four quarters

explanation.surface: A city is flooded because the defences failed to keep out the water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'quarters' gives two compass points, E and N. Venice is well known for its high-water floods.
explanation.definitionFit: Venice, built on a lagoon, is regularly swamped by high tides known as acqua alta.

clue.text: Masked raider, primarily into drugs, invades market

annotationWithheld.why: Masked raider, primarily into drugs, invades market (8): VEND (market) needs EERE inside, but R (raider primarily) into drugs gives only ERE; no reading supplies the extra E, so a word looks misread or missing
annotationWithheld.clue: Masked raider, primarily into drugs, invades market

clue.text: One pound found inside sample hat

indicators.note: found inside says the one and pound letters sit within the sample word

parts.note: to sample is to try
I is the Roman numeral one
lb is the abbreviation for a pound in weight

explanation.surface: Someone finds a pound coin tucked inside a hat being tried on.
explanation.walkthrough: A trilby is a soft felt hat with a narrow brim.
explanation.definitionFit: A trilby is a soft felt type of headwear with an indented crown.
